children: Benchmark Dutch and British wholesale gas prices were largely stable on Tuesday morning after a heavy selloff the previous day, as the market watches for any signs of diplomatic efforts at a UN meeting this week that could help reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
The benchmark Dutch front-month contract at the TTF hub (TFMBMc1) inched up by €0.10 to €73.35 per megawatt hour (MWh) by 0809 GMT, ICE data showed.
The British front-month contract (NGLNMc1) lifted by 1.00 pence to 182.60 pence per therm.
Both contracts fell around 8% on Monday to their lowest intraday levels since September 7, with losses likely overdone and correcting on Tuesday, analysts and traders said.
"Focus is on the UN meetings in New York and the possibility of US-Iran negotiations," said Arne Lohmann Rasmussen, chief analyst at Global Risk Management, in a note.

However, there is no confirmation of direct US-Iran talks and any agreement would likely require significant concessions from the US that would be difficult to accept, especially with elections looming, he added.
"Weather and Asian demand are the key for the coming month," a trader said, adding the level at which demand destruction sets in will likely set prices.

Demand for liquefied natural gas (LNG) from end-users in Northeast Asia remains weak, analysts at LSEG said in a weekly note, highlighting that customers in China, Japan and Turkey were even offering reloads or spot sales, although demand in India remained resilient.
In Europe, the weather will be drier and warmer than normal the next two weeks, LSEG meteorologist Georg Mueller said.
European gas storage last stood at 69.94% full, up 0.31 percentage points day-on-day but still 11.76 percentage points lower year-on-year, according to data from Gas Infrastructure Europe.

Norwegian gas exports remain heavily curtailed due to maintenance, with bookings dropping to 262.5 million cubic metres (mcm) per day on Tuesday, down from 273.3 mcm/day on Monday, with Wednesday to see further drops still, data from infrastructure operator Gassco showed.
In the European carbon market, the benchmark contract
was down €0.39 at €86.20 per metric ton.
